source.title: Streaming JSON Data with Multipart/Mixed and Meros

cards.question: How do you stream multiple JSON objects on one HTTP connection?
cards.answer: Use Content-Type multipart/mixed with a boundary and send each JSON object as it becomes available, instead of waiting until all data is processed.

cards.question: Why set Transfer-Encoding: chunked on a multipart JSON stream?
cards.answer: The server can send the response without knowing its total size and start flushing parts as soon as they are ready.

cards.question: What does Meros do on the client?
cards.answer: It is a JavaScript library that parses multipart streams. After fetch with Accept: multipart/mixed, you iterate each part and handle part.body.

cards.question: How does multipart streaming change a CPU-bound table-row API?
cards.answer: Without streaming, users wait until every row is calculated. With streaming, each row is flushed as soon as its calculation finishes and can appear in the UI immediately.

cards.question: How can a server stream JSON from multiple slow sources?
cards.answer: Fetch sources concurrently and write each part as any source produces data. The client can keep Maps per type and re-render as posts, comments, or users arrive.

cards.question: When should you use multipart streaming?
cards.answer: When pieces can be processed independently, each takes significant time, users benefit from partial results, or you are aggregating data from multiple slow sources.

cards.question: What resilience and memory benefits does multipart streaming provide?
cards.answer: You do not buffer a large full response, and a partial failure does not block the parts that succeeded.
